assessment_question: Who decides which teaching and production uses are permitted, restricted or excluded?
Can staff and students explain the current department AI rules?
Do module rules and visiting-tutor instructions agree with institutional policy?
Are proposed uses evaluated for educational value and preservation of craft?
Can people report harm, dispute a decision and receive a response?
Are policy changes reviewed with students and relevant specialists?
Can each AI input be traced to an appropriate permission or other documented basis for use?
Are likeness, voice, scanning, training and reuse permissions separately considered?
Are AI use and material alterations disclosed appropriately to collaborators, funders and audiences?
Are documentary truth claims, reconstructions and synthetic material clearly distinguished?
Are cultural representation, bias and community consultation considered?
Are music, archive, output rights and distribution restrictions checked before release?
Is there a maintained register of tools, features, versions and approved uses?
Do representative lab machines meet measured workflow needs?
suggested_evidence: Timed local trials and machine specs

assessment_question: Do AI assets round-trip through the department's NLE, sound and VFX workflows?
Can staff manage identities, permissions, updates and account closure?
Can projects be recovered and teaching continue during outages or model withdrawal?
Are provenance, captions, colour, audio and delivery requirements tested?
Are data destinations, retention, subprocessors and training terms understood?
Have appropriate privacy, security and DPIA screening decisions been recorded?
Can students participate without buying personal subscriptions or surrendering unnecessary rights?
Have disabled users tested the workflow and alternatives?
Are total costs sustainable at cohort scale, including failed generations and support?
Are quotas, storage, support time and environmental trade-offs managed?
suggested_evidence: Usage records and stated measurement limits

assessment_question: Can faculty distinguish assistive, generative and agentic functions and their limitations?
Can faculty complete and explain a relevant AI-assisted filmmaking task?
Can faculty detect errors, bias, continuity faults and invented sources?
Can faculty identify rights, consent and privacy issues in realistic scenarios?
Can technicians and tutors support failures and teach a workable alternative?
Is development sustained across permanent, hourly paid and visiting staff?
Do briefs specify allowed AI functions, disclosure and learning outcomes?
Does assessment reveal individual judgement, craft and authorship?
Are foundational filmmaking skills still demonstrable where required?
Can students question AI use or take an equivalent accessible route?
Are AI allegations handled fairly without treating detection scores as proof?
Does curriculum review respond to industry changes without chasing every new tool?
suggested_evidence: Reviewed mapping to skills and outcomes
